1. Introduction
The Phanerozoic evolution of the Tethyan realm involved successive dispersion, subsequent northward
drift,andeventualAsianaccretionofaseriesofGondwana‐derivedterranes(Metcalfe,2013).Thenorth-
wardmovementoftheseGondwana‐derivedterranes,whichwasaccompaniedbytheopeningorclosing
ofthe Paleo‐Tethys, Meso‐Tethys, andCeno‐Tethys, determined thedistributionof theland andsea and
affectedtheregionalandevenglobalclimatedynamics(Metcalfe,2013).Quantifyingtheriftanddrifthis-
tory of these terranes is critical for reconstructing the distribution of land and sea in the Tethyan realm
and understanding the plate tectonics history of these terranes (Song et al., 2017). For example, the
QiangtangterraneisseparatedfromtheSongpan‐GanziterranetothenorthbytheTriassicJinshasuture
zone (JSS), which marks the closure of Paleo‐Tethys, and from the Lhasa terrane to the south by the
Jurassic‐CretaceousBangong‐NujiangsuturezonebytheclosingofMeso‐Tethys(Figures1aand1b;Yin
&Harrison,2000).Therefore,theriftanddrifthistoriesoftheQiangtangterraneplayacriticalroleinunder-
standingtheevolutionofthePaleo‐TethyanandMeso‐TethyanOceans.
Currently,itiswidelyacceptedthattheQiangtangterranecanbefurtherdividedintotheNorthQiangtang
terrane (NQT) and the South Qiangtang terrane (SQT) by the Qiangtang Metamorphic Belt or the
Longmuco‐Shuanghusuturezoneduetothediscoveryoftheeclogite,blueschist,andophioliticmélange

terrane(Kappetal.,2000).Thismetamorphicbeltwassometimesconsideredtohavebeenunderthrustfrom
the JSS and exhumed in the interior of a single Qiangtang Terrane (Kapp et al., 2000). However, most
researchers suggest that the Qiangtang terrane was formed by the suturing of two independent terranes
alongtheLongmuco‐Shuanghusuture,which extendsfromnorthwesttosoutheastacrosstheQiangtang
terrane (e.g., Zhang et al., 2014, 2016). Division of the NQT and SQT can be further supported by
independent evidence from paleontological studies. The Late Paleozoic strata of the NQT contain
abundant warm‐water fossils, indicating a Cathaysian affinity (Zhang et al., 2013), whereas the Permo‐
CarboniferousstrataoftheSQTarecharacterizedbyglaciomarinedepositsandcold‐waterbiota,implying
atypicalGondwanaaffinity(e.g.,Zhangetal.,2013).
Awealthofgeologicalevidenceincludingpaleobiogeographyrecordshasbeenusedtoconstraintheorigin
andpastpositionsoftheNQT.However,theyyieldedcontradictoryinterpretations(Songetal.,2017;Zhang
etal.,2013).Forexample,Huangetal.(1992)arguedthattheNQThaddriftedawayfromtheSCBbythe
Late Permian because of its Cathaysian affinities in paleobiogeography during the Late Paleozoic.

ThedrifthistoryduringtheLatePaleozoicissignificanttounderstandingtheoriginoftheNQT.Tobetter
constrainthedrifthistoryoftheNQTanditsrelationshipwithadjacentterranes,aswellastheevolution
of the Tethys Ocean, we present a well‐dated, high‐quality paleomagnetic pole from the Late Permian

2. Geological Setting andSampling
2.1. GeologicalSetting
ThestrataoftheNQTcompriseLateDevonian‐TriassicandJurassic‐Cenozoicsedimentaryrocks,aswellas
PaleozoictoMesozoicvolcanicrocks(e.g.,Li,2015).ThePermianvolcanicandsedimentaryrocksarewidely
distributedintheeasternhalfoftheNQT.ThesePermianvolcanicshavebeenattributedtothenorthward
subductionofthePaleo‐TethysOcean.SomeofthevolcanicsmayalsobeinfluencedbytheEmeishanman-
tleplume(Liuetal.,2016).
Our study area, that is, the Zhouqiongmalu area, which is ~40 km north of the town of Yanshiping
(Figures1band1c),islocatedonthesouthoftheJSS.ThePermianstratacanbedividedintothreeforma-
tionsinthisarea(Figure1d).Theyare,frombottomtotop,theNuoribagaribaoFm(P nr),JiushidaobanFm
2
(P j),andNayixiongFm(P n).TheNayixiongFmconsistsofbasalts,basalticpyroclasticrockswithsubor-
2 3
dinate rhyolites and rhyolitic tuffs, and fine‐grained sandstones intercalated with minor tuffs. The
Palaeofusulina parafusiformis‐Nanlingella simplex fusulinid assemblage recognized in the Nayixiong Fm
indicates a Wuchiapingian (Late Permian) age (He et al., 2009). The regional structural relationships
betweenthePermianandTriassicstratasuggestthatthefoldoftheLatePermianNayixiongFmoccurred
duringthetimeintervalfromtheLatePermiantotheLateTriassic(Li,2015),mainlyduetotheTriassiccol-
lisionbetweentheNQTandtheSQT(Dan,Wang,White,etal.,2018).
2.2. Sampling
Intotal,34paleomagneticsiteswerecollectedfromtwosectionsinthesamplingarea(FigureS1ainthesup-
portinginformation).Thesetwosectionswerechosenattwolimbsoftheanticlineforapossiblefoldtest.
Twenty‐seven sites and seven sites of volcanic rocks were collected from sections A and B, respectively
(FigureS1).SevensitesfromsectionA(33.9°N,91.9°E)werecollectedasstandardpaleomagneticcoresusing
aportablegasoline‐powereddrill,andthesecoreswereorientedbybothamagneticcompassandaSuncom-
pass.Thedeclinationdifferenceislessthan2°betweenthesetwoorientingmethods,suggestingthatthe
localmagneticdisturbancecanbeneglected.Becausetheportabledrillswerebroken,theremaining27sites
werecollectedasorientedblocks.Eachsamplingsitespansseveralmetersofstratigraphicthicknessorat
leastonelavaflow.Thebeddingattitudeofbothsamplingsectionsisclear(FigureS1).Additionally,one
block sample of rhyolite was collected from the middle part of section A for zircon U‐Pb chronology
(Figure 1d). See Text S1 in the supporting information for laboratory techniques and measurements
(Andersen, 2002; Cogné, 2003; Kirschvink, 1980; Lowrie, 1990; Ludwig, 2003; Xie et al., 2008; Xiu
etal.,2001).
3. Results
3.1. ZirconU‐PbGeochronology
Mostofthezirconsfromtherhyoliteareeuhedraltosubhedralprismswithawidthnosmallerthan40μm
(FigureS2).TheTh/Uratioislargerthan0.5,indicatingthatthesezirconshaveamagmaticorigin(TableS1
inthesupportinginformation).Sixteenofthe21zirconshaveconcordantage(TableS1).Theyreliablyshow
similar206Pb/238Uages(Figure2a),yieldingaweightedaverageageof259.1±1.4Mawithmeansquare
weighted deviation = 0.77 (Figure 2b). The age of ~259 Ma determined by laser ablation sampling and
multiple‐collector inductively coupled plasma massspectrometry (LA‐MC‐ICPMS) dating methodis well
consistentwiththesecondaryionmassspectrometer(SIMS)U‐Pbzircondatingresults(~259Ma)forthe
same volcanic rock from the same bedding (Wang et al., 2018). Therefore, we confidently conclude that
theNayixiongFmvolcanicsmostlikelyeruptedat~259Ma.

4. Discussion andConclusions
4.1. PaleosecularVariation
Secularvariationmustbeaveragedoutwhenvolcanic‐basedpaleomagneticdatacanbeusedfortectonic
reconstructions.Becausethestratigraphicallyadjacentvolcanicsiteswiththesameremanencedirections
mayrecordthesamespotreadingofthepaleomagneticfield(e.g.,Lippertetal.,2014),ourpaleomagnetic
data set is evaluated for directional independence to average out secular variation by using a common
direction test (McFadden & McElhinny, 1990). Only two adjacent volcanic sites share similar directions
withinthe28sites,indicatingthatthedifferencebetweenthemeandirectionofthe28sitesandthetrue
meandirectioncanbeneglected.Theangulardispersion(S=16.4°)ofthecorrespondingVGPsofthe28
sites is similar to the dispersion of Sλ = 17.4° (limits between 12.5° and 22.5°) observed in VGP popula-
tionsfrom0to5Malavasatasimilarlatitude(Johnsonetal.,2008;TableS3).TheA (5.6°)ofthemean 95
VGPiswellwithintheN‐dependenterrorenvelope(3.2°,10.0°)proposedbyDeenenetal.(2011).These
results suggest that our new data set has averaged out paleosecular variation and thus can be used for
tectonic reconstruction.

4.2. PositionoftheNQTDuringtheLatePermian
Previous paleomagnetic investigations of Late Permian rocks of the NQT have been performed in the
RaggyorcakaareabyChengetal.(2012),intheTuotuoheareabyChengetal.(2013),andintheTuobaarea
byHuangetal.(1992).Chengetal.(2012)andChengetal.(2013)reportedtwopaleopolesfromfivesedi-
mentarysitesandfivevolcanicsites,respectively,andconcludedthattheNQTwaslocatedatdifferentpaleo-
latitudes of approximately 13.1 and −7.7°N in the Late Permian (Table S4). Other Late Permian
paleomagneticresultsof10sedimentarysitesreportedbyHuangetal.(1992)positionedtheNQTat~4.8°N
(TableS4).Allthepaleomagneticresultscontainnomorethan10sitedirectionsineachstudy.Thesecular
variationofpaleomagneticfieldcannotbefullyaveragedoutbyonlyfivevolcanicsites(Chengetal.,2013).
Besides, the possible inclination shallowing have not been tested and corrected for sedimentary data by
Chengetal.(2012)andHuangetal.(1992).Moreover,noisotopicagesareavailabletoconstraintheprecise
agesofthesepoles.Nevertheless,thesepioneeringinvestigationsconstraintheNQTlocatedatornearthe
equatorinthetropicsduringtheLatePermian.
TheNayixiongFmpaleomagneticdataofournewresultsarefrom28volcanicsiteswithoutinclinationshal-
lowingandfulfillthequalitycriteriaofVanderVoo(1990),Deenenetal.(2011),andJohnsonetal.(2008).
Inaddition,previousstudiesontheNayixiongFmvolcanicrocksobtainedtheFisher(1953)meandirection
offivesitesatDs=250.1°,Is=14.9°,ks=37.3,andα =12.7°aftertiltcorrection(Chengetal.,2013).The
95
inclination(correspondingtopaleolatitude)isnearlyequaltothatcalculatedfromthe28sitesinournew
data.Giventhatthesite‐meandirectionsreportedbyChengetal.(2013)includedirectionsdeterminedusing
theremagnetizationgreatcircleplanefittingtechniques,whicharenotasreliableastheHTCdirections
determinedusingprincipalcomponentanalysis,weonlyusedournewdatafortectonicreconstruction.
Notably,ourpaleomagneticresultsoftheNayixiongFmvolcanicsrevealedthat149(27)of184tilt‐corrected
directions have a downward (upward) inclination with a westward declination. When a (sub) equatorial
paleolatitude is observed, the choice between normal and reversed polarity is often ambiguous (Huang
etal.,1992).Theageofthemiddlepartofoursamplingsectionisdatedat~259Ma,whichisconsistentwith
theage(~259–256Ma)determinedbySIMSU‐Pbzircondating(Wangetal.,2018)andhasreversedpolarity
(Oggetal.,2016).Therefore,weconcludedthatoursamplingareawasmorelikelylocatedatapaleolatitude
of−7.6±5.6°Nat~259Ma.GiventheaccuracyanduncertaintyofanalyticaltechniquesinzirconU‐Pbgeo-
chronology,wecannotfullyexcludethepossibilityofnormalpolaritycharacteristicremanentmagnetiza-
tiondirectionsformostofthevolcanicsamplingsites(27sites)inthisstudy.Inthiscase,theNQTwould
belocatedat7.6±5.6°NintheLatePermian.Nevertheless,ineithercase,ournewpaleomagneticresults
reveala(sub)equatorialpaleolatitudeintheLatePermianfortheNQT.
4.3. TheNorthwardMovementoftheNQT
Few paleomagnetic results from the Permian and Triassic rocks from the Qiangtang terrane have been
reported, mainly due to a lack of proper sections for paleomagnetic sampling (Cheng et al., 2012, 2013;
Lin&Watts,1988;Songetal.,2012;Yangetal.,2017;Ye&Li,1987).Wehavesummarizedavailabledatain
TableS4insupportinginformation(Figure1b).Toobtainreliablereconstruction,weonlyusedthesedata,
whichfulfillthefollowingcriteria,asSongetal.(2017)haveapplied:(1)positivefieldteststhatconstrainthe
ageofmagnetization,(2)theobservedpaleolatitudeiscalculatedfrom10ormoresite/groupmeandirec-
tionsforvolcanicrocksorfrom100ormoresampledirectionsforsedimentaryrocks,and(3)theA for 95
thestudypassestheDeenenetal.(2011)criteria.OnlythreepaleomagneticresultsfromSongetal.(2015,
2017)and this study fulfillthese criteria (Figure3 and Table S4). Songet al. (2015, 2017) obtained high‐
quality, well‐dated paleomagnetic results of the Early Permian and Late Triassic ages, which come from
manyvolcanicsiteswithclearbeddingattitudes.Thesehigh‐qualitypaleomagneticresultshaveshownthat
theNQTwaslocatedat−22.1±4.7°Nat~297Maand31.5±3.0°Nat~209Maforthereferencepointat
(33.9°N,91.9°E).Thispaleolatitudeevolutionrevealsa~53.6°latitudinal(~5,900km)northwardmovement
intheTethysOceanfromthetropicalpaleolatitudeofthesouthernhemisphereintheEarlyPermiantothe
subtropicalpaleolatitudeofthenorthernhemisphere,untilitcollidedwiththeNorthChinablockandTarim
inthenorth(Songetal.,2015,2017).
TheobservedpaleolatitudeoftheLatePermianfurthersupportedthisgradualnorthwardmovementand
showed that the NQT was located at −7.6 ± 5.6°N at ~259 Ma (Figures 3a and 3d). Notably, the

paleolatitudeoftheNQTintheLatePermianissimilartothatofthecoevalSouthChinablock,whichwas
locatedatan equatorialpaleolatitude(Huangetal.,2018; Metcalfe, 2013).The similarpaleolatitudesare
consistent with the similarities of shared Permian fauna and flora (He et al., 2009; Zhang et al., 2013),
demonstratingthattheywereincloseproximityatthattime(Metcalfe,2013;Zhaoetal.,2018).Theproxi-

gered their breakup (e.g., Chung et al., 1998). Because the Late Permian bimodal volcanic rocks and
oceanic‐island basalt‐like mafic rocks related to the plume‐subduction interaction were identified in the
northeasternmarginoftheNQT(e.g.,Liuetal.,2016;Wangetal.,2018),theNQTwasprobablylocated
onthesouthwestoftheEmeishanlargeigneousprovinceoftheSCBbasedonourpaleomagneticresults
(Figures3aand3d).Additionally,the paleolatitudeofthe NQTissimilartothat ofthe southernmargin
oftheSCBattheEarlyPermian(Huangetal.,2018;Songetal.,2017;Zhaoetal.,1996).Allthesescenarios
implyacontinentalconnectionbetweentheNQTandtheSCBasearlyastheEarlyPermian.Tosummarize,
the paleomagnetic, paleontological, and magmatic constraints indicated that the NQT moved northward
togetherwiththeSCBduringthePermian.
4.4. FurtherImplicationfortheOriginoftheNQT
Song et al. (2017) suggest that the NQT rifted from the Greater India margin of Gondwana prior to the
PermianandmovednorthwardduringthePermianandTriassicperiodsbasedonthepaleomagneticcon-
straints at this time. The further question is how did it rift from the Greater India margin of the
Gondwana.DiditmovenorthwardtogetherwiththeSQT?Noreliablepaleomagneticresultsareavailable
to constrain the paleolatitude of SQT at the Late Paleozoic. However, the Permo‐Carboniferous strata of
theSQTarecharacterizedbyglaciomarinedepositsandcold‐waterbiota,implyingatypicalGondwanaaffi-
nity (e.g., Zhang et al., 2013). This means that the SQT was still located at the northern margin of the
GondwanaintheEarlyPermian.However,atthesametime,theNQTdriftedawayfromthenorthernmar-
ginofGondwana(Songetal.,2017).ThepaleogeographicreconstructionintheEarlyPermiansuggeststhat
theNQTandtheSQTwereseparatedbyanancientocean(Zhaoetal.,2018;Figure3c).Theexistenceofthis
oceanhasbeenconfirmedbythePermianandCarboniferousophiolitesincentralQiangtang(Zhangetal.,
2016).ThisconclusionisconsistentwiththemarkedlydifferentmagmatismintheNQTandtheSQTduring
theLatePaleozoictoTriassic(Zhaietal.,2013).TheTriassicarcmagmatismexposedinthesouthernmargin
oftheNQTwasattributedtothenorthwardsubductionoftheLongmuCo‐ShuanghuOcean.Notably,no
arc‐typemagmatismcanbefoundintheSQTduringtheLatePaleozoictoTriassic(Zhaietal.,2013).The
magmatismoftheSQTwasrelatedtoamantleplume,whichmayhavetriggeredtheinitialriftingofthe
SQTfromtheGondwanamargin(Liaoetal.,2015).TheseanalysesindicatethattheNQTwasseparated
fromtheSQTwhenitriftedfromthenorthernmarginofGondwana.BecausetheSQTwasstronglyinflu-
encedbythecold‐tocool‐temperateconditionsandwarmclimateconditionsthroughoutthePermian,it
was regarded as a drifting median plate, drifting northward from Gondwana to Cathaysia during the
Permian(Zhangetal.,2013).However,fewreliablepaleomagneticresultsareavailabletoconstrainhow
the SQT drifted and accreted to the NQT. Notably, Song et al. (2012) reported paleomagnetic data from
theNQTandtheSQTwithpositivefoldandreversaltestsandobtainedsimilarpaleolatitudes(~29°N)for
bothintheLateTriassic,whichindicatesthattheNQTandtheSQTformedasingleunitatleastasearly
astheLateTriassic(Songetal.,2012;Figure3e).Thisisconsistentwiththeage(~233Ma)oftheeclogite‐
faciesmetamorphismofPianshishaneclogitesincentralQiangtang(Dan,Wang,White,etal.,2018).
When did the NQT rift off Gondwana? The paleolatitude difference of ~32.6° between the NQT and the
expected Gondwana at the earliest Permian suggests that the NQT rifted off Gondwana prior to the
Permian(Figure3a).ThepaleolatitudeevolutionatPermianshowsthattheNQTmovednorthwardatarate
of~4.2cm/yearduring~297–259Ma.Extrapolatingaconstantnorthwardvelocityhasbeenwidelyusedin
tectonic applications of paleomagnetism (e.g., Lippert et al., 2014). The paleolatitude evolution of the
Gondwanan‐Indian northern margin prior to 320 Ma remains poorly constrained. Assuming that the
NQT maintained a stable paleolatitude before it drifted away from the Greater India margin of
Gondwana, the paleolatitude difference between the NQT and Gondwana would decrease to zero at

Geophysical Research Letters 10.1029/2018GL080964
~382Mawhenextrapolatingtherateof~4.2cm/yearduringthePermiantopre‐Permian,implyingdisper-
sionoftheNQTatthistime.GiventhelargeuncertaintyofthepaleolatitudeevolutionofGondwana,we
tentatively concluded that the NQT rifted off the Greater Indian margin of Gondwana in the Devonian
(Figures3aand3b).ThisconclusionisconsistentwiththattheLateDevonianvolcanicarcdevelopedin
thesouthernmarginoftheNQT(Dan,Wang,Zhang,etal.,2018).Notably,morereliablepaleomagneticdata
fromDevonianandCarboniferousstrataoftheNQTandtheGreaterIndiamarginofGondwanaarecritical
toconstraintheriftingprocess.
4.5. Conclusions
Wehaveprovidedrobustandwell‐datedpaleomagneticresultsfromtheLatePermianNayixiongFmvolca-
nicsintheNQT.Thesedataaverageoutsecularvariationandthuscanbeusedforreconstruction.Ournew
results show that the NQT was located at equatorial paleolatitude (−7.6 ± 5.6°N) at the late Permian
(~259 Ma). Combined with paleontological and magmatic constraints, our results reveal that the NQT
driftednorthwardtogetherwiththeSCBduringthePermianandthattheNQTdriftedawayfromthenorth-
ernmarginofGondwanaintheDevonian,whichisearlierthanthedeparturetimeoftheSQT.
